match.reason: The bank point teaches sound devices in poetry such as alliteration and assonance, while the new point teaches diegetic and non-diegetic sound in film, which is a different idea.

draft.title: Diegetic and non-diegetic sound
card: sound that comes from the world of the story. The characters could hear it too, such as dialogue, footsteps or a radio playing in a room.
sound added for the audience that the characters cannot hear, such as a music soundtrack or a narrator's voice-over.
To tell them apart, ask: could the people in the scene hear this? If yes, it is diegetic. If no, it is non-diegetic.
Non-diegetic sound shapes mood. Slow, low music can build fear or sadness, and fast music can build excitement. Diegetic sound makes the scene feel real.
draft.remember: Diegetic sound is heard by the characters. Non-diegetic sound is added for the audience to shape mood.

a.q: In a film scene, two friends talk while a tune plays on a radio in their kitchen. Which sound is diegetic?
opts: The radio tune, because the friends can hear it
The radio tune, because it is music
The friends' talk, because it is not music
Neither, because both are recorded in a studio
a.why: The radio is part of the kitchen, so the friends could hear it. That makes it diegetic. Being music does not make a sound non-diegetic: what matters is whether the characters can hear it.
a.clue: Ask whether the people in the scene could hear it.

b.q: A girl walks alone down a dark street. Slow, low music rises that she cannot hear, and the audience feels afraid. What is the music and its effect?
opts: Non-diegetic sound that builds fear in the audience
Diegetic sound that shows the girl is afraid
Non-diegetic sound that the girl can hear nearby
Diegetic sound that makes the street seem real
b.why: The girl cannot hear the music, so it is non-diegetic. It is added for the audience and shapes their mood. Diegetic sound would come from the street itself, and it would make the scene feel real rather than build fear.
b.clue: Can the girl hear the music?

a.best: The radio tune, because the friends can hear it

b.best: Non-diegetic sound that builds fear in the audience

problems.detail: The question asks 'Which sound is diegetic?' as if only one is, but by the card the friends' talk (dialogue) is also diegetic. The option 'The friends' talk, because it is not music' names a sound that really is diegetic, only with a wrong reason. Students who know the idea may be confused. Reword it, for example 'Why is the radio tune diegetic?'

The stem gives the answer away. It says the music is something 'she cannot hear' and that 'the audience feels afraid', which restates both halves of the right option, so a student can match the words without knowing the idea.

Why (b) says diegetic sound 'would make the scene feel real rather than build fear'. This is a false generalisation: diegetic sounds such as footsteps, creaks or a scream can build fear and suspense. Mood-building should not be presented as something only non-diegetic sound does.

The card says non-diegetic sound shapes mood and diegetic sound makes the scene feel real. This implies diegetic sound does not shape mood, which can mislead students. A softer line such as 'diegetic sound can also build mood' would avoid this.

check.summary: Question a treats only one sound as diegetic, though the friends' dialogue is diegetic too. Question b's stem restates the answer, and why (b) wrongly suggests diegetic sound cannot build fear.

proposal.title: Diegetic and non-diegetic sound
card: sound that comes from the world of the story. The characters could hear it too, such as dialogue, footsteps or a radio playing in a room.
sound added for the audience that the characters cannot hear, such as a music soundtrack or a narrator's voice-over.
To tell them apart, ask: could the people in the scene hear this? If yes, it is diegetic. If no, it is non-diegetic.
Both kinds can shape mood. A soundtrack of slow, low music can build fear, and so can a door creaking in a quiet house.
proposal.remember: Ask whether the characters could hear it: yes means diegetic, no means non-diegetic.

a.q: In a film scene, two friends talk while a tune plays on a radio in their kitchen. Why is the radio tune diegetic?
opts: The friends in the kitchen could hear it
It is music playing in the background
It is added to shape the audience's mood
It was recorded separately from the talking
a.why: The radio is part of the kitchen, so the friends could hear it. That makes it diegetic. Being music in the background does not decide it: what matters is whether the characters can hear the sound.
a.clue: Think about who in the scene can hear the tune.

b.q: A girl walks alone down a dark street. Slow, low music rises, but no radio, band or speaker is anywhere in the scene. What is the music?
opts: Non-diegetic sound that can build fear in the audience
Diegetic sound that can build fear in the audience
Non-diegetic sound that the girl hears as she walks
Diegetic sound that comes from the street around her
b.why: The music has no source in the world of the story, so the girl could not hear it. That makes it non-diegetic, and slow, low music can build fear. Diegetic sound can build fear too, but it comes from the scene itself, such as her footsteps.
b.clue: Where in the scene could the music be coming from?

a.best: The friends in the kitchen could hear it

b.best: Non-diegetic sound that can build fear in the audience
